root.label: Instantiation and specialization
root.note: Each argument set names a specialization, instantiated from the template or written by hand.

children.label: Implicit instantiation
children.note: Happens on demand when a use needs the definition.

children.label: Declarations only
children.note: A class instantiation creates member declarations, not member function bodies.

children.label: Bodies when used
children.note: A member function, default argument or static member is instantiated only if needed.

children.label: Pointers need nothing
children.note: Naming Box<T>* or Box<T>& does not instantiate the class.

children.label: Point of instantiation
children.note: Where dependent names are resolved as though the specialization were written.

children.label: Function templates
children.note: Right after the namespace-scope declaration that uses it, and also at end of file.

children.label: Class templates
children.note: Immediately before the namespace-scope declaration that needs it.

children.label: Differing meanings
children.note: If two points give different meanings, ill-formed, no diagnostic required.

children.label: Explicit instantiation
children.note: You tell the compiler to instantiate, or not to.

children.label: template struct X<int>;
children.note: Instantiates every member defined at that point, so all bodies must compile.

children.label: extern template
children.note: Suppresses implicit instantiation of non-inline definitions in this translation unit.

children.label: Missing definition
children.note: Used but never explicitly instantiated anywhere: ill-formed NDR, usually a link error.

children.label: Explicit specialization
children.note: template<> supplies the definition for one exact argument list.

children.label: Unrelated class
children.note: A full class specialization inherits no members from the primary template.

children.label: Single member
children.note: One member function of an implicit specialization can be specialized alone.

children.label: Declare before use
children.note: After an instantiating use, or missing in another TU: ill-formed NDR.

children.label: Partial specialization
children.note: Constrains the shape of arguments while keeping some parameters.

children.label: Class and variable
children.note: Allowed for class templates and, since C++14, variable templates only.

children.label: Most specialized wins
children.note: Among matching partial specializations; equal ones make the use ambiguous.

children.label: Exact matching
children.note: int* const does not match T*; cv-qualifiers are part of the type.

children.label: Function templates
children.note: No partial specialization; overload them instead.

children.label: Not in overload resolution
children.note: Only primaries compete; the winner's explicit specialization then supplies the body.

children.label: Dimov/Abrahams
children.note: A specialization attaches to the best primary visible where it is declared.

children.label: Prefer overloads
children.note: Use a plain overload, or forward to a partially specialized class template.
